description: 🚀 PARAKRAM | AI, coding & space enthusiasts building an interactive Astronaut Mission Trainer. Looking for passionate teammates to innovate and explore beyond limits! 🌌
summary:
OUTPOST ZERO is an interactive, educational mission trainer that simulates the challenges of establishing and sustaining a human outpost beyond Earth. It transforms complex space exploration concepts into an engaging mission-control experience where users can monitor outpost systems, manage critical resources, respond to simulated emergencies, and make decisions as a Junior Astronaut or Flight Director.

The project combines NASA space science resources with interactive simulations, mission telemetry, and scenario-based learning. Users explore how factors such as power availability, environmental conditions, crew needs, and resource constraints influence mission decisions. The experience is designed to make space exploration more accessible to students and space enthusiasts while encouraging systems thinking, scientific curiosity, and decision-making.

OUTPOST ZERO is an educational simulation, not an operational spacecraft system. Its goal is to help users understand the complexity of future lunar and planetary exploration through an immersive, hands-on digital experience.
details:
OUTPOST ZERO: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive space exploration and outpost management simulation designed to make the challenges of human space exploration understandable and engaging.

git hub- https://github.com/deepeshpankaj01/OUTPOST-ZERO

The project provides a mission-control-style interface where users can experience two roles: Cadet and Flight Director. Users interact with mission scenarios, monitor simulated outpost telemetry, manage resources, explore crew and habitat systems, and respond to mission events. The simulation emphasizes the interconnected nature of mission systems: decisions involving power, resources, environmental conditions, and crew operations can affect mission stability and outcomes.

The platform also integrates NASA’s space science resources, including NASA’s DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information) where applicable, to introduce users to real space-related data. Scientific information and simulation assumptions are intended to be distinguished so that users can understand what is based on published sources and what is modeled for educational gameplay.

The project is designed for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. Its intended impact is to promote STEM learning, space science awareness, systems thinking, and decision-making through an immersive digital experience rather than passive reading.

Technology Stack:
• Next.js 14 and React for the web application
• TypeScript for application logic
• Tailwind CSS for responsive styling
• Framer Motion for animations and interactive experiences
• Recharts and SVG for telemetry visualization
• NASA DONKI API for relevant space-weather information
• LocalStorage for saving user progress

Creative Approach:
OUTPOST ZERO combines a mission-control interface, resource management, interactive scenarios, and educational space science into a browser-based mission trainer. The experience is designed to make complex exploration challenges approachable while keeping the user actively involved in mission decisions.

The application is an educational simulation. It is not an official NASA product, NASA-endorsed system, or real spacecraft operations tool. Simulated values and scenarios are not intended for actual mission planning or safety decisions.
